easy.def: A word that shows something is inside or within.
examples: The milk is in the fridge.
We swim in the pool.
I was born in May.

more.def: A word used to show that something is inside a place, a shape, a group, or a time.
examples: The fish swim in the deep part of the lake.
Our class stood in a circle.
Leaves turn red and gold in autumn.

easy.def: To make someone or something a part of a group.
examples: Please include me in your game.
The lunch includes an apple.
We include everyone in our club.

more.def: To have as a part, or to make something part of a group.
examples: The price of the ticket includes a drink and a snack.
The tour includes a visit to the castle.
Be sure to include your name on your paper.

easy.def: Very hard to believe; amazing.
examples: The view was incredible.
It was an incredible jump.
What an incredible story!

more.def: So amazing or surprising that it is hard to believe.
examples: The view from the mountain was incredible.
She made an incredible jump.
The magician did an incredible trick.

easy.def: Really; for sure.
examples: It is indeed cold.
Yes, indeed!
Indeed, I am hungry.

more.def: Used to show that something is really true.
examples: It was indeed the best day of my life.
The test was hard indeed.
Yes, indeed, we are ready to go.

easy.def: Facts about something.
examples: I need information about frogs.
The sign gives information.
Ask for information.

more.def: Facts or details about something.
examples: The library has information about every state.
Read the sign for information about the park.
I found information about frogs in a book.

easy.def: Not having done anything wrong.
examples: The boy was innocent.
I am innocent.
The dog looked innocent.

more.def: Not guilty of a crime or wrongdoing; not having done what you are blamed for.
examples: The detective proved that the boy was innocent.
I am innocent because I did not touch the cookies.
The innocent dog sat quietly.

easy.def: Very silly or wild.
examples: That idea is insane.
An insane amount of snow.
The ride was insane.

more.def: Very wild or extreme. In its medical meaning, it should be used carefully.
examples: The amount of snow was insane.
That roller coaster is insane.
It is an insane plan to cross the river on a log.

easy.def: A small bug with six legs.
examples: An ant is an insect.
A bee is an insect that can sting.
The insect sat on a leaf.

more.def: A small animal with six legs and a body in three parts, often with wings.
examples: Bees, ants, and butterflies are all insects.
Some insects, like crickets, make sounds with their wings.
An insect's body has three main parts.

easy.def: In the inner part of something.
examples: The cat is inside the box.
Look inside the bag.
We stayed inside the tent.

more.def: In or into the inner part of something.
examples: There is a surprise inside the small box.
The kitten curled up inside my coat.
He kept the secret inside his heart.

easy.def: In a house or building.
examples: Let us go inside.
We play inside.
It is cold, so stay inside.

more.def: Into or within a house or other building.
examples: It started to rain, so we went inside.
The dog barked until we let him inside.
We stayed inside all day because of the snow.

easy.def: To say something strongly.
examples: I insist on helping.
She insisted on paying.
He insists he is right.

more.def: To say firmly that something must be done or is true.
examples: I insist that you take the last piece.
She insisted on helping with the dishes.
He insists that he saw a fox.

easy.def: In place of something.
examples: I took an apple instead.
Let us walk instead.
She had tea instead of milk.

more.def: In place of something else.
examples: It was raining, so we played inside instead.
I wanted pizza, but we had soup instead.
He walked instead of taking the bus.

easy.def: A thing you play to make music.
examples: A drum is an instrument.
What instrument do you play?
A flute is an instrument you blow.

more.def: An object used to make music; also, a tool for careful work.
examples: The violin is her favorite instrument to play.
Every instrument in the band plays a different part.
The dentist used a small instrument to check my teeth.

easy.def: Money you pay so that you get help if something bad happens.
examples: We have car insurance.
Insurance paid for the damage.
The house has insurance.

more.def: An agreement in which you pay money so that you will be paid if something bad happens.
examples: Dad pays for car insurance each month.
Insurance covered the cost of the repairs.
The family has insurance for their house.

easy.def: To plan to do something.
examples: I intend to go.
She intends to win.
He intended to call.

more.def: To have something in mind to do.
examples: I intend to finish my homework before dinner.
She intended to surprise her mother.
He intended to call but forgot.

easy.def: A wish to know more.
examples: She has an interest in space.
He lost interest.
He shows interest in bugs.

more.def: A feeling of wanting to learn about or take part in something.
examples: She has a big interest in dinosaurs.
He lost interest in the game.
My interest in music began at age five.

easy.def: Something you like to do.
examples: My interests are art and soccer.
Her interests include chess.
He has many interests.

more.def: Something that you enjoy doing or learning about.
examples: Her interests include painting and swimming.
Chess is one of his main interests.
We share an interest in birds.

easy.def: Wanting to know more.
examples: I am interested in space.
She was interested in the book.
He is interested in birds.

more.def: Wanting to learn about or take part in something.
examples: I am interested in learning to play the guitar.
She seemed interested in the bug on the leaf.
Are you interested in joining the choir?

easy.def: Making you want to know more.
examples: This is an interesting book.
The story is interesting.
I found an interesting bug.

more.def: Holding your attention and making you want to learn more.
examples: The museum had an interesting display of old coins.
That was the most interesting book I have read.
She told us an interesting fact about whales.

easy.def: To stop someone when they are talking or busy.
examples: Please do not interrupt me.
Do not interrupt when I am on the phone.
The bell interrupted our game.

more.def: To stop someone while they are speaking or doing something.
examples: A loud knock interrupted the teacher in the middle of the story.
Sorry to interrupt, but dinner is ready.
A power cut interrupted the movie.

easy.def: A talk where someone asks questions.
examples: The reporter did an interview.
Mom had a job interview.
The interview was short.

more.def: A meeting in which someone asks a person questions.
examples: The reporter did an interview with the winner.
Mom has a job interview on Monday.
The interview was on the radio.

easy.def: To ask someone questions.
examples: I interviewed my grandpa.
She interviews the winner.
He interviewed the mayor.

more.def: To ask someone questions in order to learn about them.
examples: I interviewed my grandfather for a school project.
The reporter interviewed the winner.
She interviews people for a magazine.

easy.def: A word that shows going to the inside.
examples: The cat jumped into the box.
We walked into the room.
Put the toys into the bin.

more.def: A word used to show movement to the inside of something, or a change to another form.
examples: The frog leaped into the pond with a splash.
A caterpillar turns into a butterfly.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake it.

easy.def: To tell people each other's names.
examples: Let me introduce my friend.
She introduced me to her mom.
He introduced himself.

more.def: To tell people each other's names when they meet for the first time.
examples: Let me introduce you to my cousin.
The teacher introduced the new student to the class.
He introduced himself to the neighbors.

easy.def: To make something that no one has made before.
examples: I want to invent a robot that cleans my room.
She invented a new game.
Who invented the bike?

more.def: To think of and create something new for the first time.
examples: People invented the wheel thousands of years ago.
He invented a machine that feeds the cat.
The children invented a secret code for their notes.

related.def: To make something again in a new way.

easy.def: Looking carefully to find out the facts.
examples: The police began an investigation.
The investigation took days.
A careful investigation.

more.def: A careful search to find out the facts about something.
examples: The police began an investigation of the lost bike.
Scientists carried out an investigation of the old tree.
The investigation took three days.

easy.def: To ask someone to come.
examples: I will invite my friends to my party.
Our teacher invited a vet to class.
Invite your sister to play.

more.def: To ask someone to come somewhere or to do something with you.
examples: We invited our new neighbors over for dinner.
The neighbors invited us to their barbecue.
She was invited to speak at the meeting.

easy.def: To have something as a part.
examples: The game involves running.
Baking involves measuring.
This job involves lots of walking.

more.def: To include something as a necessary part.
examples: Playing the piano involves a lot of practice.
The project involves building a model volcano.
Camping involves sleeping in a tent.
